newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Clark says fewer disagreements with NZ First.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Clark says fewer disagreements with NZ First.

text.p: Labour leader Helen Clark said on Wednesday Labour's meeting with New Zealand First was shorter than National's because there were fewer disagreements and Prime Minister Jim Bolger talked more.
"There are fewer disagreements and I don't talk as much as he does," Clark said.
NZ First leader Winston Peters said Clark's explanation "was a logical explanation for some things and not for others."
"It is fair to say people are more voluble in the mornings,"Peters said.
Asked about progress, Clark said she was pleased with Wednesday afternoon's two and a half hour meeting.
"We are into a lot of detail. Positively," Clark said.
National held a three hour meeting with NZ First on Wednesday morning which Bolger said included detailed negotiation on policy.

The main opposition Labour Party and the conservative National Party are holding separate talks over the shape of the next government with nationalist NZ First, which holds the balance of power after the October 12 election.
Parliament must meet by December 13. The parties have said they hope to form a government before then.
Clark was quoted in the Evening Post newspaper as saying National would compromise anything to get into power.

"Some would. I think there are some on the backbench who see that as fundamentally against what they have stood for and taken a lot of abuse for over the last six years," Clark said after the meeting.

Asked if Labour was having to make concessions, she said: "We wouldn't be sitting in that room if we didn't think we could come out with a coalition agreement that kept faith with our policy." -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473 4746
